resources.string: Few answers so far: the result may not be reliable.
Many players reported that this game does not work on %1$s. It can still be installed.
This game is not in the library.
The game is raised so it matches the standing height, even while seated.
GamePort measures where the head really is and works out how far to raise the game from the chosen height.
Steam lists the arguments this game can be started with. A plain switch for VR is picked at first, the others are only offered, and a game that does not know an argument ignores it.
Picked from what Steam lists for VR
This game has no settings on this device.
The game is patched with the latest version
Connects the game to the Steam account and adds cloud saves and seated mode. Only the copy on this device changes.
The patch is removed: the game runs as it comes from Steam
The game will run without GamePort: no Steam account (achievements, multiplayer), no Steam Cloud saves and no seated mode. The patch can be applied again at any time, and nothing is downloaded.
A game that keeps flashing a permission window or closes on its own needs access to files and media, allowed here.
This game asks for access to the device\'s files. Without it, it may close on its own. The game\'s permissions allow files and media access.
A newer patch is available for this game.
This game asks for access to files and does not have it. It may close on its own.
Saves differ between this device and Steam: a choice is needed.
This game keeps its saves on Android apart from the PC ones: they are not synced with the PC version. GamePort can bring the PC saves here.
The last save sync could not reach Steam: the saves were not synced.
The last save sync failed: the latest saves may not be on Steam.
Installing the patched game… Android may ask for a confirmation.
The game has to be started once for GamePort to see its saves.
In sync: this device and Steam hold the same saves.
This device, seen %1$s (at the last launch of the game)
Steam Cloud could not be reached: its side may be out of date.
The next time the game starts, Steam\'s saves will replace the ones on this device. A safety copy of this device\'s saves is kept first.
The next time the game starts, this device\'s saves will replace the ones on Steam, and on every other device too. A safety copy of Steam\'s saves is kept first.
At the next launch of the game, Steam\'s saves replace this device\'s.
This game keeps its saves on Android apart from the PC ones: they are not synced with the PC version.
This game keeps its saves on Android apart from the PC ones: they are not synced with the PC version. GamePort can bring the PC saves here.

For a test or a clean start, with the game closed. Nothing is removed from Steam: this device\'s saves are put aside right away in a backup on the device, then the next launch of the game brings back what Steam holds, following the options above.
This device\'s saves are moved now to a backup folder on the device, and nothing is removed from Steam. A save that was not sent to Steam yet then stays in that backup only. The game must be closed.
%1$d file(s) put aside in the device\'s backup. Steam was not touched.
This device\'s saves could not be put aside. The game must be closed and patched with the latest GamePort.
The studio keeps the PC saves of this game apart from the Android ones, so Steam does not share them between a PC and this device. They can be brought here.
Steam holds no PC saves of this game.
Lists the saves Steam keeps for PC below, instead of the Android ones. Nothing changes.
Each time the game starts, the PC saves are brought to this device, which sends them on to the Android saves. Nothing is written to the PC.

From now on, each time the game starts, the PC saves are brought to this device, and this device\'s saves are backed up before they are replaced. This device then keeps feeding the Android saves as usual. Nothing is written to the PC saves. If both the PC saves and this device changed since the last time, a choice is asked. This stays on until switched off.
Needs the option above. This device also writes to the PC saves, which could damage them. A clean copy of them is made first and kept.

This device\'s saves are then also sent to the PC saves, and the PC takes them over. The Android version may write its saves differently, which could damage the PC ones. A clean copy of the PC saves is made now and kept. Playing, making a save, then checking on the PC that it loads is the safe way to find out, and the copy puts the PC saves back if it does not.
This device also writes to the PC saves.
The PC saves feed this device each time the game starts.
Clean copy of the PC saves, made %1$s: %2$d file(s).

The PC saves return to what the clean copy held. Files sent from this device since then are replaced or removed in Steam, and the PC takes them over at its next sync. This device goes back to the Android saves.
Making the clean copy of the PC saves…
The clean copy could not be made, so nothing changed. Steam Cloud may be out of reach.
The PC saves could not be put back. Steam Cloud may be out of reach, or the copy is damaged.
At the next launch of the game, this device\'s saves replace Steam\'s.
A new version of this game is available.
Each control and where it goes are listed below. A control is remapped by selecting it, then choosing its destination in the list.
On: the choices below apply to this game.
This game has no controls for this device\'s controllers. The Steam Frame\'s controls are put on them by default, and can be customised if some do not work well.
Available once the Steam Frame\'s controls are put on this device\'s controllers.
Force the detection of the Steam Frame\'s controllers
Useful when the game starts but does not react to the controllers. Changes nothing if the game has no controls for the Steam Frame\'s controllers.
No control for the Steam Frame\'s controllers was seen the last time the game ran. Trying anyway is possible, and if nothing changes, switching it off is safer.
A button of this device then does several things at once: %1$s. Customising the controls below can change it.
Several buttons can be ticked, and none means nothing happens.
The choices for this game are erased and GamePort\'s mapping applies again.
This game has no controls for this device\'s controllers: the %1$s ones are emulated and can be remapped.
The game seems to start well, but it does not seem to react to the controllers. If that is the case, turning on support for the Steam Frame\'s controls may help.
Support for the Steam Frame\'s controls is on for this game, from its next start. If nothing changes, it can be turned off with the controllers button on the game\'s page.
This game comes in several versions and none fits this device on its own. Choose the one to install.

A copy of this game is already installed on this device, probably the one from the Meta store. The two cannot be installed together. Using this version means uninstalling the other one first, and its saves on this device are lost with it.
This game belongs to another GamePort on this device (%1$s). It is started and updated from there.
This game is already installed by another GamePort on this device (%1$s). It can stay with that one, or be uninstalled so this GamePort installs it.
Uninstall it and install this version
This sends the project a technical file that helps find why %1$s does not work, with no personal data. A ticket on GitHub can be opened too.

It contains the versions of GamePort, of the game and of its patch.
The device and its system.
The player's choices for the game, and how it ran, frame rate included.
The game's files and everything inside its APK.
The Steam interfaces it asks for.
The game's log, its start and its latest lines, and GamePort's.
How its last runs ended, with the crash report Android kept.
What GamePort did for it, such as the download, the patch and the install.
Account numbers, e-mail addresses, network addresses and the account name are removed from the text files.
This game closed almost right away. A report can help find out why.
This game seems to have crashed. A report can help find out why.
This game has expansion files that an earlier patch named after a raised version, which can stop it from starting. Does the game work?
Uninstall the game and install it again?

The game is removed from this device, then downloaded and installed again from scratch, which can take a while and use mobile data. Saves that were sent to Steam Cloud come back with it. Other data the game kept on this device is removed.
The game disappears from the app only. Nothing changes on Steam, and an installed game stays installed.\nHidden games are listed in Settings, under Hidden games, where each can be shown again.
Read from the Steam account. Nothing is changed on Steam from here.
Useful when recentering does not bring the game back in front. The game then uses the play space that recentering moves, with the floor at the right height. Where the content stands may change.
Done automatically for this game: the headset has no play area.
Let the game show the real world

A game that can show the real world behind it may not be allowed to by the headset, because its VR build does not say it uses it. Turning this on declares it for this game. Automatic does it for the games known to need it. It is for a game that has a passthrough setting that does not work. A change patches the game again.

Some games ask for it, and the system of some devices stops the game when the device has no eye tracking. Automatic keeps it where the device has eye tracking and leaves it out where it has none. Off leaves it out for this game, on keeps it. Applies at the next start of the game.
Done automatically for this game: its VR build does not say it uses the passthrough.
Smooth out a game that stutters

Some games carry mixed reality scripts from Meta without the library they call, and stutter because they fail at every update. By default the game is given a small stand-in that answers for the missing library. Turning it off is for a game that does not work that way. A change patches the game again.
Open the game itself in VR

Some games start with a first screen that then opens the game itself. By default the game itself opens in VR too, instead of in a flat window. Turning it off is for a game that does not work that way. A change patches the game again.
A few words help a lot: the report shows how the game ran, not what was seen.
The report will be sent as soon as this device is online.
The report could not be sent.
No report could be made for this game.
Preview: made-up values, nothing is installed
This game has large files beside its app, and GamePort cannot check that they are all there. If it lacks content or does not start, repairing downloads them again.

The game\'s large files are downloaded again and put back in place, which can take a while and use mobile data. The game stays installed and its saves are not touched. It cannot be played until this is done.
